title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: A meta-analytic review of the testing effect.
finding: Testing beats restudy on later retention; initial recall tests give larger benefits than recognition tests, which supports effortful retrieval as the cause.
implication_for_bucket: Bucket's three-choice recognition quiz is the weaker form of retrieval; typed recall should be the default.
notes: Abstract gives no pooled effect; effect left null. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
population: Students across school and university samples
method_studied: Practice testing against restudy and other controls
finding: Practice tests beat restudy and every other comparison condition; test format, sample and outcome type moderate the size.
implication_for_bucket: Supports quiz-first study; the internal claim of g about 0.51 must cite the paper's table, which this pass did not open.
notes: Abstract states no number. core.jsonl cites g≈0.51 from the paper body; unconfirmed here. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Testing (quizzing) boosts classroom learning: A systematic and meta-analytic review.
finding: Classroom testing raises achievement to a medium extent; exposure, transfer-appropriate processing and motivation each explain part of it.
implication_for_bucket: Classroom-grade evidence that a daily quiz moves achievement by about half an SD.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Transfer of test-enhanced learning: Meta-analytic review and synthesis.
method_studied: Transfer of retrieval practice to new questions and contexts
finding: Testing yields transferable learning against a re-exposure control; transfer depends on response congruency, elaborated retrieval practice and initial test performance.
effect: d = 0.40, 95% CI [0.31, 0.50] (192 effect sizes, 122 experiments, N = 10,382)
contested: Transfer is weakest to untested material seen during study and to rearranged items; bias-corrected intercepts often indicate no transfer when the three moderators are absent.
implication_for_bucket: A retest on the same items overstates learning; Bucket needs held-out transfer items.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis.
method_studied: Spacing and lag between study episodes
finding: Spaced beats massed study, and the gap that maximises retention grows as the retention interval grows.
implication_for_bucket: No single spacing percentage exists; the optimal gap is a function of the target retention interval.
notes: Abstract reports counts only, no pooled effect. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Spacing Effects in Learning: A Temporal Ridgeline of Optimal Retention
population: More than 1,350 adults online, gaps up to 3.5 months, tests up to 1 year
method_studied: Gap between study and review as a function of test delay
finding: The optimal gap is a falling share of the test delay.
effect: Optimal gap about 20 to 40% of a 1-week delay, falling to about 5 to 10% of a 1-year delay
implication_for_bucket: Gives a sourced rule for review intervals at a chosen retention horizon, such as Bucket's 90-day horizon.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: A Meta-Analytic Review of the Benefit of Spacing out Retrieval Practice Episodes on Retention
method_studied: Spaced against massed retrieval; expanding against uniform schedules
finding: Spaced retrieval beats massed retrieval by a large margin; expanding schedules show no advantage over uniform ones.
effect: Spaced vs massed g = 0.74 (39 effect sizes); expanding vs uniform g = 0.034, not significant (54 effect sizes)
contested: Expanding-interval superiority, a premise of SM-2 style growth, is not supported on average.
implication_for_bucket: The gain comes from spacing retrieval at all; interval growth curves need their own evidence.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators.
finding: Interleaving helps inductive learning, most for visual categories; blocking wins for word lists.
effect: Overall g = 0.42; paintings g = 0.67; mathematics g = 0.34; words g = -0.39
contested: The effect reverses for words and is ambiguous for expository text.
implication_for_bucket: Interleave confusable problem types; keep vocabulary items blocked or spaced instead.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: A randomized controlled trial of interleaved mathematics practice.
population: 54 seventh-grade mathematics classes, preregistered cluster RCT over 4 months
finding: On an unannounced test one month later the interleaved group outscored the blocked group.
effect: 61% vs 38% correct, d = 0.83
implication_for_bucket: Mixed-skill assignments are the strongest preregistered classroom result in the set and fit Bucket's daily route.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Learning Concepts and Categories: Is Spacing the “Enemy of Induction”?
method_studied: Spaced or interleaved against massed exemplars for category induction
finding: Induction profited from spacing although learners rated massing as more effective even after seeing their own results.
implication_for_bucket: Learner preference is a poor guide; self-chosen blocking should not be the default.
notes: Abstract gives no effect size. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
finding: Self-explanation prompts raise learning across task types and subjects.
effect: g = 0.55 (69 effect sizes)
implication_for_bucket: A 'why is this true' prompt after an answer is cheap and supported.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Promoting self-explanation to improve mathematics learning: A meta-analysis and instructional design principles
finding: Prompting gives small to moderate gains in procedural knowledge, conceptual knowledge and procedural transfer immediately after study; evidence for classroom use and delayed retention is limited.
contested: Delayed and classroom effects are 'much more limited' by the authors' own account.
implication_for_bucket: Bucket's 'why' line should be tested at a delay before it is counted as learning.
notes: Abstract gives no number. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Structuring the Transition From Example Study to Problem Solving in Cognitive Skill Acquisition: A Cognitive Load Perspective
method_studied: Fading worked steps toward independent problem solving

implication_for_bucket: Supports a depth ladder that removes support as mastery rises.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: A Meta-analysis of the Worked Examples Effect on Mathematics Performance

finding: Worked examples raise mathematics performance by a medium amount.

contested: Expertise reversal applies: the benefit shrinks or reverses for advanced learners (see literature:kalyuga-2003-expertise-reversal-effect).
implication_for_bucket: New atoms should open with a worked example before the first quiz item.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The generation effect: A meta-analytic review
method_studied: Generating an item against reading it
finding: Generated information is remembered better than read information.
effect: d = 0.40 (86 studies, 445 effect sizes)
contested: Moderator variance was substantial.
implication_for_bucket: Typed or constructed answers beat recognition; supports generated-answer quizzes over three-choice items.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Learning Versus Performance: An Integrative Review
population: Review of motor and verbal learning research

finding: Performance during acquisition is an unreliable index of learning; some manipulations raise one and lower the other, and learners misread fluent performance as learning.
implication_for_bucket: In-session accuracy and streaks measure performance; only delayed tests measure learning.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: When Problem Solving Followed by Instruction Works: Evidence for Productive Failure
method_studied: Problem solving before instruction against instruction first
finding: Problem solving first gives a moderate advantage, larger with high fidelity to productive-failure design; the trend reverses for second to fifth graders.

contested: Contrasting trends for second to fifth graders, per the abstract.
implication_for_bucket: A problem-first step suits adult learners on conceptual atoms, with instruction following the attempt.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The effects of feedback interventions on performance: A historical review, a meta-analysis, and a preliminary feedback intervention theory.
finding: Feedback raises performance on average but over one third of interventions lowered it; feedback loses value as it draws attention to the self.

implication_for_bucket: Feedback must point at the task; praise, rank and person-level messages are the risk.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Focus on Formative Feedback
finding: Feedback effects depend on learner and task; the review ends with guidelines such as specific, task-focused, elaborated feedback.
implication_for_bucket: A source for the feedback rules behind the 'why' line and the learn-this link.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research
finding: Feedback has a medium average effect with high heterogeneity; it cannot be treated as one treatment.
contested: Lowers the Hattie and Timperley figure near 0.79 held in the corpus.
implication_for_bucket: Replace the corpus figure d near 0.79 with 0.48 and state the heterogeneity.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Effects of Feedback in a Computer-Based Learning Environment on Students’ Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis

finding: Explanations beat showing the correct answer, which beats right or wrong marking.

implication_for_bucket: A green or red bar alone is worth about nothing; every item needs an explanation.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The effect of type and timing of feedback on learning from multiple-choice tests.

finding: Delayed feedback led to better final-test performance than immediate feedback.
contested: Kulik and Kulik 1988 find classroom quiz studies usually favour immediate feedback while laboratory studies favour delayed.
implication_for_bucket: Feedback timing is a parameter to test, with a delayed review of missed items as one arm.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Mastery Learning Reconsidered
population: Group-based mastery learning in elementary and secondary schools, at least 4 weeks
finding: Best-evidence synthesis found no support on standardized measures and moderate effects on experimenter-made measures that did not persist.
effect: Essentially no effect on standardized achievement measures
contested: Contradicts Kulik, Kulik and Bangert-Drowns 1990 (ES 0.52, literature:kulik-kulik-bangert-drowns-1990-mastery-learning-meta-analysis).
implication_for_bucket: A mastery gate must be judged on independent tests, since most of its measured effect sits on tests built by the experimenter.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Educational Outcomes of Tutoring: A Meta-analysis of Findings

implication_for_bucket: The pre-Bloom tutoring estimate; it also supports learning by teaching.
notes: Abstract gives no number. von Hippel 2024 reports this meta-analysis as about 0.33 SD. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The Promise of Tutoring for PreK–12 Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Experimental Evidence
population: Randomized field experiments of preK-12 tutoring
finding: Tutoring gives consistent positive impacts, largest with teacher or paraprofessional tutors, early grades, three or more days a week and during school.
effect: Pooled ES 0.288 SD (SE 0.029, p < .001)
contested: The NBER version of 2020 reported 0.37 SD (literature:nickow-2020-impressive-effects-tutoring-prek).
implication_for_bucket: This is the unnamed 'AERJ 2024' reference in the corpus; use 0.29 SD as the tutoring benchmark.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: What Impacts Should We Expect From Tutoring at Scale? Exploring Meta-Analytic Generalizability
method_studied: Tutoring effects under scale and independent tests

contested: Third downward re-estimate of the two-sigma claim.

notes: Crossref lists the journal version in Review of Educational Research with a 2026 date; first circulated as a 2024 working paper. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Formative Assessment: A Meta-Analysis and a Call for Research
population: 13 K-12 studies with 42 effect sizes, from more than 300 screened

title: Formative assessment: a critical review

title: Active learning increases student performance in science, engineering, and mathematics

implication_for_bucket: Passive reading of an atom is the lecture condition; every atom needs an act.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Problem-Based LearningisCompatible with Human Cognitive Architecture: Commentary on Kirschner, Sweller, and Clark (2006)

implication_for_bucket: Sets out the three frames Bucket must choose among when it states its aim.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Creating Capabilities: The Human Development Approach
finding: Asks what each person is able to do and to be, and judges development by real opportunities instead of GDP.
implication_for_bucket: Under this frame learning counts when it widens what the person can do in life.
notes: No page-level quotation was verified. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Public Goods, Private Goods: The American Struggle Over Educational Goals
finding: Democratic equality, social efficiency and social mobility compete, and the growth of the mobility goal turns education into a private good.
implication_for_bucket: A credential product serves the mobility goal; Bucket should say which goal it serves.
notes: Cited in the corpus by URL; DOI confirmed here. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Interpreting Effect Sizes of Education Interventions
population: Distribution of effects from causal education studies with standardized outcomes
finding: Effects that are small by Cohen's standards are large for field interventions; interpretation must include study features, cost and scalability.
contested: Kraft 2023 answers critics of fixed benchmarks.
implication_for_bucket: Bucket should judge its own effect against field trials, where a tenth of an SD is meaningful.
notes: The numeric benchmarks sit in the paper body and were not confirmed from the abstract. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The Effect-Size Benchmark That Matters Most: Education Interventions Often Fail
population: Randomized trials of education interventions with standardized achievement outcomes
finding: Most efforts to improve education move scores little.
effect: 36% of effect sizes are below 0.05 SD
implication_for_bucket: A null result is the base rate; preregister and report it.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: How to Engage in Pseudoscience With Real Data: A Criticism of John Hattie’s Arguments in Visible Learning From the Perspective of a Statistician
finding: Argues that averaging effect sizes across unlike comparisons and outcomes is statistically invalid.
contested: Directed at Hattie 2009.
implication_for_bucket: Do not rank methods by a pooled d from mixed designs.
notes: Abstract is an editorial note; the summary follows the title and the paper's stated purpose. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The misdirection of public policy: comparing and combining standardised effect sizes
method_studied: Comparing and combining standardized effect sizes
finding: Standardized effect size depends on comparison group, sample range and measure, so league tables rank research designs more than interventions.
implication_for_bucket: The ranking in this corpus is a rough order; like-for-like comparisons need the same outcome and control.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: How Methodological Features Affect Effect Sizes in Education
finding: Published, small and experimenter-measured studies report effects about twice as large; quasi-experiments exceed randomized trials.
effect: Effect sizes roughly twice as large for published, small-scale and experimenter-made-measure studies
implication_for_bucket: Halve any effect that comes from a small study with its own test, which describes most learning-method evidence.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Rigorous Large-Scale Educational RCTs Are Often Uninformative: Should We Be Concerned?
population: 141 large RCTs, 1,222,024 students, EEF and NCEE
finding: Mean effects are small and the intervals wide.
effect: Mean 0.06 SD; mean CI width 0.30 SD; median Bayes factor 0.56
implication_for_bucket: Size a Bucket trial to detect 0.1 SD or expect an uninformative result.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Persistence and Fade-Out of Educational-Intervention Effects: Mechanisms and Potential Solutions
venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
population: Review of educational interventions with follow-up
finding: Fade-out is widespread, substantive, and coexists with persistence; persistence depends on the skills targeted and later environments.
implication_for_bucket: Measure at follow-up; an end-of-course gain is likely to shrink.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Fadeout and persistence of intervention impacts on social–emotional and cognitive skills in children and adolescents: A meta-analytic review of randomized controlled trials.
method_studied: Persistence of cognitive and social-emotional impacts
finding: Posttest impacts predict follow-up impacts similarly for both skill types at 6 to 12 months and less at 1 to 2 years.
implication_for_bucket: Plan follow-ups at 6 to 12 months and again later.
notes: Abstract truncated before the persistence coefficients. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Visible Learning
finding: Synthesises meta-analyses into a ranking of influences and a model of visible teaching and learning.
contested: Bergeron and Rivard 2017 and Simpson 2017 reject the pooling method.
implication_for_bucket: Use the underlying meta-analyses, not the league table.
notes: The d = 0.40 hinge point is in the book body and is not recorded here. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Does Far Transfer Exist? Negative Evidence From Chess, Music, and Working Memory Training
population: Meta-analyses of chess, music and working-memory training in children
method_studied: Far transfer to cognitive and academic skills
finding: Effects are small to moderate and shrink as design quality rises; far transfer rarely occurs.
effect: Effect sizes inversely related to design quality
implication_for_bucket: Claim near transfer only; 'learning how to think' claims need active-control evidence.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Near and Far Transfer in Cognitive Training: A Second-Order Meta-Analysis
finding: Training gives near transfer; far-transfer effects are small or null.
effect: Far transfer 'small or null' (k = 233)
implication_for_bucket: Same as above, with the largest evidence base.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Working Memory Training Does Not Improve Performance on Measures of Intelligence or Other Measures of “Far Transfer”: Evidence From a Meta-Analytic Review
finding: Near measures improve; with treated controls there is no convincing far transfer.
effect: No reliable far-transfer effect with treated controls
implication_for_bucket: Active controls remove the effect, so Bucket's trial needs one.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Do “Brain-Training” Programs Work?
venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
population: Intervention studies cited by brain-training companies
finding: Extensive evidence of gains on trained tasks, less on closely related tasks, and little on distant tasks or everyday performance.
implication_for_bucket: The template for auditing a learning product's own claims.
notes: Abstract truncated before its final clause; the last part of the summary follows the review's known conclusion. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: The cognitive benefits of learning computer programming: A meta-analysis of transfer effects.
finding: Programming instruction transfers, more to near than to far measures.
contested: A far-transfer estimate well above the cognitive-training literature; most studies lack active controls (not stated in the abstract).
implication_for_bucket: A counter-case: structured domain instruction may transfer further than drills.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Long-term retention of basic science knowledge: a review study
population: General and medical education retention studies
finding: About two thirds to three quarters of knowledge remains after one year and slightly under half after two.
effect: Two thirds to three quarters retained at 1 year; slightly below 50% at 2 years
implication_for_bucket: Gives unassisted forgetting baselines at 1 and 2 years for a Bucket retention target.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Comparison of normalized gain and Cohen’sdfor analyzing gains on concept inventories
finding: Normalized gain is biased in favour of groups with higher pretest scores.
implication_for_bucket: Report standardized gains with pretest as covariate, and avoid normalized gain for comparisons.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Validity of psychological assessment: Validation of inferences from persons' responses and performances as scientific inquiry into score meaning.
finding: Validity is one concept with content, substantive, structural, generalizability, external and consequential aspects.
contested: Borsboom et al. 2004 argue validity is only whether the attribute causes the scores.
implication_for_bucket: A mastery score needs evidence on all six aspects, including what happens when people act on it.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Validating the Interpretations and Uses of Test Scores
finding: It is the interpretation and use of a score that is validated; bolder claims need more evidence, and consequences count.
implication_for_bucket: 'Mastered at 0.7' is a claim that needs its own argument and evidence.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Applications of Item Response Theory To Practical Testing Problems
finding: Sets out item response models and their use for test construction, equating and adaptive testing.
implication_for_bucket: The base reference for calibrating items so scores are comparable across forms.
notes: Abstract is a catalogue line; DOI is the Routledge reissue. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Machine Learning–Driven Language Assessment
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
method_studied: Machine-learned item difficulty for adaptive testing
finding: Item difficulty can be estimated from language models without human piloting, giving reliable scores that align with other high-stakes tests.
contested: Authored by Duolingo staff.
implication_for_bucket: A route to large item banks; it still needs an external criterion.
notes: Abstract gives no coefficient. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Measuring the Impacts of Teachers II: Teacher Value-Added and Student Outcomes in Adulthood
population: More than one million children, school and tax records
finding: Students of high value-added teachers attend college more, earn more and have fewer teenage births.
effect: Replacing a bottom 5% teacher with an average one raises a classroom's lifetime income by about $250,000 in present value
contested: Rothstein 2017 disputes the sorting assumptions (not included; unverified in this pass).
implication_for_bucket: Test-score gains can carry into adult outcomes even when scores fade.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Early Childhood Intervention and Life-Cycle Skill Development: Evidence from Head Start
population: Siblings in the NLSY, Head Start participants
finding: Participants gain on a young-adult outcome index despite test-score fade-out.
effect: 0.23 SD on a summary index of young adult outcomes; one third of the median to bottom-quartile income gap
implication_for_bucket: Long-run indices can show effects that test scores stop showing.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Measuring human capital using global learning data
finding: Learning progress has been limited despite rising enrolment; human capital measured by learning explains a fifth to a half of income differences.
effect: Human capital explains one fifth to one half of cross-country income differences
implication_for_bucket: Enrolment and completion are weak proxies for learning.
notes: Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Transfer of Training: A Meta-Analytic Review
method_studied: Predictors of transfer to the job
finding: Cognitive ability, conscientiousness, motivation and a supportive work environment predict transfer; same-source measurement inflates the relationships.
implication_for_bucket: Workplace transfer must be rated by someone other than the learner.
notes: Abstract gives no coefficient. Title and authors matched to the Crossref record for this DOI.

title: Democracy and Education: An Introduction to the Philosophy of Education
finding: "It is that reconstruction or reorganization of experience which adds to the meaning of experience, and which increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience." (ch. 6). Also: "the educational process has no end beyond itself; it is its own end" (ch. 4).
implication_for_bucket: Under Dewey, something is learned when it changes how the person directs later experience, which a recall score does not show.
notes: Both quotations checked against the Gutenberg full text on the verification date. Chapter numbers given; the ebook has no page numbers. Replaces the blog-sourced Dewey line in the corpus.

title: My Pedagogic Creed
finding: "education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living" (Article II); "education must be conceived as a continuing reconstruction of experience; that the process and the goal of education are one and the same thing" (Article III).
implication_for_bucket: A product that defers all value to a later credential runs against this definition.
notes: Quotations checked against the Wikisource text; the transcription prints 'aa' for 'as' in the second line, corrected here. Article numbers follow the essay's structure and were not checked against a page image.

title: Pedagogy of the Oppressed
finding: Freire contrasts a 'banking' model, where the teacher deposits content in passive students, with problem-posing education in which teacher and students inquire together into their world. Paraphrase; no quotation was verified.
implication_for_bucket: A deck of atoms delivered for recall is the banking form; learner-posed questions are the alternative.
notes: Open Library confirms author, title and 1970 first publication. The text was not opened, so the finding is a paraphrase without page.

title: Development as Freedom
finding: Development is treated as the expansion of the real freedoms people have, with education as one of the social opportunities that build capability. Paraphrase; no quotation was verified.
implication_for_bucket: Counts learning by what it lets the person do and choose.
notes: Open Library confirms author, title and 1999 first publication. Text not opened.

title: The Tacit Dimension
finding: Polanyi argues that people know more than they can tell and that skilled knowing rests on particulars the knower cannot fully state. Paraphrase; no quotation or page was verified.
contested: Collins 2010 (Tacit and Explicit Knowledge, doi 10.7208/chicago/9780226113821.001.0001) separates relational, somatic and collective tacit knowledge.
implication_for_bucket: The primary source for the corpus's unsourced claim that apprenticeship carries tacit knowledge; it is a philosophical argument with no measurement.
notes: Open Library confirms author, title and 1966 first publication. Text not opened.

title: Taxonomy of Educational Objectives: The Classification of Educational Goals. Handbook I: Cognitive Domain
population: Handbook by a committee of college examiners
finding: Classifies cognitive objectives into six classes from knowledge to evaluation. Paraphrase; the class list is confirmed through Krathwohl 2002 and not from the handbook itself.
contested: Revised in 2001; see krathwohl-2002-revised-bloom-overview and literature.jsonl (Anderson 2001).
implication_for_bucket: The source of the depth-ladder idea; Bucket's four depths are its own and unvalidated.
notes: Open Library confirms title and first author; its record lists first publication as 1961 for the edition it holds. Co-authors and the 1956 date are from the standard citation and were not confirmed.

title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 26
finding: "Education shall be directed to the full development of the human personality and to the strengthening of respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms." (Article 26.2).
implication_for_bucket: The oldest international statement puts personal development ahead of qualification.
notes: Quotation checked against the UN page.

title: International Standard Classification of Education: ISCED 2011
finding: Education is defined as the processes by which societies deliberately transmit their accumulated information, knowledge, understanding, attitudes, values, skills, competencies and behaviours across generations; it involves communication designed to bring about learning.
implication_for_bucket: The statistical definition requires deliberate, organised communication, which Bucket's product meets; self-directed informal learning falls outside it.
notes: The UIS PDF returned 403 and 404. The UNESCO-UNEVOC glossary (connect.unevoc.unesco.org, term 'education') confirms the opening clause through 'understanding' and attributes it to ISCED 2011, 2012; the remainder is from search snippets. Paragraph and page numbers were not verified.

title: OECD Learning Compass 2030: Concept Note
venue: OECD Future of Education and Skills 2030
concept_defined: Aim of education and student agency
finding: The framework sets individual and collective well-being as the aim and defines student agency as the capacity to set a goal, reflect and act responsibly to effect change. Wording from search snippets of the OECD student agency page.
implication_for_bucket: Agency is a stated outcome that an app's guided route does not exercise unless the learner sets the goal.
notes: oecd.org returned 403 and the concept-note PDF host did not resolve. Wording comes from web-search snippets and a secondary citation, so no page number is given.

title: Theory of knowledge guide (first assessment 2022)
population: Diploma Programme core course for ages 16 to 19
concept_defined: Theory of knowledge as a curriculum
finding: A required Diploma Programme course in which students examine how knowledge claims are made and justified across areas of knowledge, assessed by an exhibition and an essay. Structure details were not verified against the guide.
contested: Hughes 2014 finds the course's assessment covers critical thinking unevenly.
implication_for_bucket: The closest existing curriculum to a theory-of-knowledge canon; Bucket has no outcome evidence for it and should not claim one.
notes: ibo.org returned 403 and a hosted copy of the guide returned 404. Existence, publisher and year come from a secondary citation; hours, word limits and weights are not recorded because they could not be confirmed.

title: SuperMemo 2: Algorithm (from Optimization of learning, Master's thesis, University of Technology in Poznan)
finding: Intervals are I(1) = 1 day, I(2) = 6 days, then I(n) = I(n-1) x EF, with the easiness factor starting at 2.5, adjusted by a 0 to 5 self-grade and floored at 1.3. The formula 'was constructed heuristically'.
implication_for_bucket: SM-2 is a heuristic with no trial behind its constants, the same status as most Bucket parameters.
notes: Formula and wording checked against the author's page.

title: SRS Benchmark
population: 9,999 Anki collections, 349,923,850 evaluated reviews (without same-day reviews)
finding: FSRS-6 predicts recall better than half-life regression and DASH; FSRS-5, which Bucket codes, is worse than FSRS-6; small neural models beat every FSRS version.
contested: Maintained by the FSRS authors; the metric is prediction calibration on Anki users, with no retention or efficiency outcome for learners.
implication_for_bucket: The benchmark supports moving from FSRS-5 to FSRS-6 and shows the corpus's '700M-review' claim matches an older dataset description (about 727 million reviews).
notes: Figures read from the repository README on the verification date; the table changes as versions are added. No SM-2 row was found in the fetched tables.

title: Two-Sigma Tutoring: Separating Science Fiction from Science Fact
population: Review of Bloom 1984 and later tutoring evidence
finding: Bloom's figure came from two dissertations using narrow tests, extra feedback and trained tutors; 'About one-third of a standard deviation seems to be the typical effect of an intense, well-designed program evaluated against broad tests.'
effect: About one third of an SD typical; Cohen, Kulik and Kulik 1982 about 0.33 SD; Nickow et al. 2020 0.37 SD, none of 96 studies reached two sigma
implication_for_bucket: Resolves the corpus contradiction: two sigma is a ceiling from narrow tests, and a third of an SD is the planning figure.
notes: Quotation and figures checked against the article text.

title: Changing Mindsets: Effectiveness trial
population: 101 schools and 5,018 Year 6 pupils in England, September 2016 to February 2017
method_studied: Growth mindset workshops over eight weeks
finding: A school-randomized effectiveness trial of growth mindset teaching; the EEF press summary reports no additional progress in literacy or numeracy.
contested: The 2015 pilot had reported promising results.
implication_for_bucket: The largest independent UK trial of mindset teaching found nothing.
notes: Design, sample and authors checked on the NIESR page. The null result comes from web-search snippets of the EEF press release (EEF pages returned 403), so effect is left null.

title: Duolingo Effectiveness Study: Final Report
population: Adult Spanish learners using Duolingo for about eight weeks
finding: A commissioned pre-post study with no control group reported gains on a placement test per hour of study.
contested: Krashen's critique notes attrition (90 of 156 finished), an older and more educated sample, and Duolingo funding.
implication_for_bucket: Duolingo's founding efficacy claim rests on an uncontrolled, funded study with 42% attrition.
notes: The PDF could not be fetched (TLS error). Krashen's critique and press coverage report 8.1 WebCAPE points per hour of study with SD 12.1; these are secondary and are not entered as the effect.

title: Memory: A Contribution to Experimental Psychology (trans. Ruger and Bussenius, 1913)
venue: Teachers College, Columbia University; Classics in the History of Psychology
method_studied: Forgetting measured by savings in relearning
finding: The founding forgetting-curve study, measured on the author with nonsense syllables.
contested: Replicated by Murre and Dros 2015 with one subject.
implication_for_bucket: The curve under every scheduler comes from single-subject data on meaningless material.
notes: Title, translators and publisher checked against the York University index page; chapter data were not opened.

authors: National Council on Measurement in Education
title: Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing
concept_defined: Validity, reliability and fairness of tests
finding: The joint standards that define the evidence a test needs for its intended interpretation and use; open access since 2021 per the publisher page.
implication_for_bucket: The checklist Bucket's assessment and credential would be held to.
notes: Existence, sponsors and the 2014 edition checked on the open-access page. No definition was quoted because the PDF was not opened.
